audit_question: Does current HSConfig still operate as a narrow pre-run skill after the source-informed apply gate work, with operator UX centered on docs/operator/README.md and reports/operator_summary.json, while HSTuner, replay, winrate, and post-run tuning concerns remain excluded?

primary_sources.evidence: States that HSConfig is pre-run only, excludes replay and winrate concerns, and defines the normal path as source-manifest -> draft-source-documents -> research-deck -> prepare -> operator_summary.json -> apply only when requested.
Defines the normal operator path, keeps operator_summary.json as the single normal gate, and narrows source-informed apply to the ALLOWED_SOURCE_INFORMED lane with explicit readiness checks.
Defines HSConfig as pre-run only, routes the operator to docs/operator/README.md, and restricts apply to the enforced operator summary gate.
Matches the repo skill boundary and documents the same source-informed apply restriction and HSTuner exclusion.
Keeps the workflow pre-run, marks hdt_deck_id as identity-only metadata, and says source-informed apply is still not SOURCE_BACKED_STRONG.
Root help says HSConfig builds packages before games are played and separates the normal path from expert and legacy paths.
Prepare is labeled Normal package creation path.
Apply exposes only package, runtime-root, allow-source-informed, and json flags, with no replay or post-run surfaces.
Allows apply only for SOURCE_BACKED_STRONG or the explicit source-informed ready profile, blocks by default otherwise, and rejects optional normal-path surfaces such as Presume.json and Concede.json.
Computes SOURCE_INFORMED_APPLY_READY only for limited blocker reasons and keeps runtime-surface, combo, condition, mechanic, conflict, uncovered-card, and low-confidence issues as blockers.

primary_sources.command: python -m pytest -q tests/test_scope_boundaries.py tests/test_cli_help.py tests/test_operator_guidance.py tests/test_skill_sync.py tests/test_skill_files.py tests/test_apply_gate.py
primary_sources.evidence: 65 passed in 1.58s on 2026-07-08, confirming current docs, help text, skill sync, scope boundaries, and apply gate behavior.
Reported that the installed HSConfig skill is in sync with the repo source.
Defines the representative 11-deck proof set with nine core_source_backed_fixture rows and two source_informed_valid_fixture rows.

confirmed_facts: README.md, docs/operator/README.md, the repo skill, the installed skill, and the workflow reference all describe HSConfig as pre-run only and explicitly exclude replay parsing, winrate inspection, runtime-log analysis, candidate promotion, and after-game tuning.
The normal operator entry point remains docs/operator/README.md, and the normal command path remains source-manifest -> draft-source-documents -> research-deck -> prepare -> apply.
reports/operator_summary.json remains the single normal operator gate for handoff or apply decisions; lower-level reports are explanatory evidence and not independent apply authority.

The source-informed apply change did not open a general warning-based write path. apply_gate.py only allows apply when the package is SOURCE_BACKED_STRONG, or when allow_source_informed is explicitly set and operator_summary.json is in the SOURCE_INFORMED_APPLY_READY / ALLOWED_SOURCE_INFORMED / readiness=ready state.

operator_summary.py restricts source-informed readiness to narrow blocker reasons: cards_need_guide_claims and cards_need_mulligan_claims. Runtime-surface gaps, combo-sequence gaps, condition or mechanic lowering gaps, conflicts, uncovered cards, and generic low-confidence cards still block that lane.
apply_gate.py and its tests keep normal-path runtime output lean by rejecting Presume.json, Concede.json, nested runtime files, stale summary file lists, and missing operator summary structure.
CLI help still presents prepare as the normal package creation path and build as the expert lower-level path, which preserves the intended operator UX split after the gate work.
The installed skill is currently synchronized with the repo source, so the live operator-facing skill matches the audited boundary.

The 11-deck representative matrix is still framed as pre-run proof coverage: nine rows are already core_source_backed_fixture, while Kingslayer and Boarlock remain source_informed_valid_fixture rows that expose missing pre-run source-to-runtime links rather than post-run tuning needs.
strengths: The negative scope is repeated consistently across README, operator docs, repo skill source, installed skill, workflow reference, and scope tests.
Operator UX is lean: one normal doc entry point, one normal command path, one first report to open, and a clear split between normal and expert paths.
The source-informed apply lane is narrow and explicit instead of becoming a broad warning-based runtime write escape hatch.
Enforcement is not documentation-only. Current code and passing tests actively block out-of-scope or structurally unsafe apply cases.
The representative deck matrix still supports a pre-run configuration proof model rather than drifting into HSTuner-style post-run evidence handling.
gaps_or_risks: The root and subcommand help surfaces are intentionally short and do not restate the full negative boundary, so operators still depend on docs/operator/README.md and the synced skill text for the full scope contract.

The source-informed apply path adds a real runtime write capability for valid-but-not-strong packages, so any future drift between operator_summary semantics, apply_gate enforcement, and skill/docs wording could weaken the lean boundary if not kept under test.
The CLI still exposes expert and legacy surfaces in the same binary; the separation is clearly labeled today, but that UX relies on sustained wording discipline rather than on separate executables.

eleven_deck_implications.summary: The current 11-deck proof set still supports a lean pre-run HSConfig boundary. Nine decks already prove SOURCE_BACKED_STRONG inside the normal pre-game package workflow. Kingslayer and Boarlock are explicitly kept as source-informed-valid pre-run gap rows that should close remaining source-to-runtime links before promotion, not as reasons to add replay parsing, winrate analysis, HSTuner follow-up, or post-run tuning logic to HSConfig.

recommendation: Keep the current boundary and operator UX as the default contract. The next practical hardening step is to add one short negative-scope sentence to apply help or root help that repeats that source-informed apply remains pre-run only and does not move replay, winrate, or HSTuner concerns into HSConfig.
